title: Desktop resume of a gateway session ignores `model_config.gateway_runtime` and recombines the model with the stale `billing_provider` → 404
before: At parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the affected parent files are the versions present in the checkout. Gateway turns persisted the live model and a nested `model_config.gateway_runtime` route, while `sessions.billing_provider` represented the first-accounted billing route. The Desktop/TUI stored-session reader read the row model, top-level provider/endpoint/wire fields, and then fell back to `billing_provider` when the top-level provider was absent; it did not read the nested gateway route. A row whose model had moved to provider B could therefore resume as that model plus provider A. The CLI resume reader already delegated route resolution to the shared canonical reader.
after: At 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, the shared persisted-route reader keeps nested `gateway_runtime` ahead of top-level TUI route fields and, when no nested route is selected, fills a missing top-level provider from a routable `billing_provider` without overwriting an explicit top-level provider or accepting bare billing buckets. Desktop/TUI resume now consumes that reader for `provider`, `base_url`, and `api_mode` as one route, so a current gateway model is restored with its current route and stale top-level or first-call billing values no longer win. Existing model selection, reasoning/service-tier handling, profile exemptions, foreign-endpoint handling, and stale-provider healing remain outside the changed behavior.
diff: Implementation-bearing three-file change, +33/-24. `hermes_state_gateway.py` changes the shared route merge by 6 additions and 6 deletions; `tui_gateway/server.py` removes its local billing-provider precedence and uses the shared route by 6 additions and 18 deletions; `tests/tui_gateway/test_resume_switched_provider_endpoint.py` adds two focused regression tests with 21 additions. The gateway write path, session schema, and billing-accounting implementation are not changed by this commit.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned ref is an implementation-bearing commit with parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe; its subject explicitly identifies the gateway-runtime resume fix for issue 125942 and the salvaged change 125956.
The pinned commit changes exactly three files and reports 33 additions and 24 deletions: the shared session route reader, the Desktop/TUI reader, and one existing resume test file.
evidence_units.source: Pinned commit file tree and diff summary; [commit diff](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480)

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` derived the model from the row, provider from top-level `model_config.provider` or `billing_provider`, and endpoint/wire fields from top-level `model_config`; it had no lookup of `gateway_runtime`.
evidence_units.source: Checkout parent-equivalent `tui_gateway/server.py`, `_stored_session_runtime_overrides`, around lines 1554-1610; parent blob 466f3becd40d580b21a1ed0a8144557acc66c2bb

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` already preferred a nested runtime with a provider, then returned top-level provider/base_url/api_mode, then returned a routable billing provider; a top-level route lacking provider was returned without being completed from billing_provider.
evidence_units.source: Checkout parent-equivalent `hermes_state_gateway.py`, `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime`, lines 776-806; parent blob a15f92e6ee3d70350a61e84e4dd876ab2ef5cb01

evidence_units.claim: The gateway producer persists the live route per turn: `_sync_session_model_from_agent` collects provider, base_url, api_mode, and fallback state into `gateway_runtime`, then updates the stored session metadata and model.

The billing columns can remain stale relative to a later gateway route because `update_token_counts` treats the first accounted usage as `first_accounted_route`, rewrites the session model and billing provider once, and then retains the one-row billing record.

The CLI resume path already calls `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime` and uses its returned provider/base_url/api_mode route, establishing the canonical cross-surface reader that the Desktop/TUI path should share.
Desktop/TUI resume modes call `_stored_session_runtime_overrides` before creating or restoring the agent, including deferred, cold, and eager resume paths.

The pinned server diff replaces the local provider/billing/endpoint selection with `SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row)` and maps the returned provider, base_url, and api_mode together, while retaining service-tier and later validation/healing logic.

The pinned shared-reader diff changes the fallback merge so a routable billing_provider fills only a missing top-level provider via `setdefault`, while explicit top-level route fields remain and nested gateway_runtime remains the highest-precedence route.

The pinned test additions cover the reported mismatch and stale-top-level precedence: one row has a current model, stale billing_provider, and only nested gateway_runtime and asserts Desktop and CLI resolve the same current route; another has stale top-level provider/endpoint values and asserts the nested gateway route wins.

The pre-existing endpoint regression uses real temporary SessionDB rows for a gateway model switch or an older row and verifies that resume does not combine the current provider with a previous provider's endpoint.

The issue evidence and pinned commit identify the base failure as Desktop restoring `anthropic` with no endpoint instead of the nested `openai-codex`/`codex_responses` route, and report the two focused regression tests as red on base and green on the implementation head.

candidate_atomics.name: canonical_route_fallback_merge
candidate_atomics.description: Complete the shared persisted-session route contract for legacy top-level route metadata without changing nested-route precedence or treating a bare billing bucket as a provider identity.

semantic_action.intent: Keep a stored provider, endpoint, and wire mode coherent when top-level session metadata contains endpoint information but omits its provider.
semantic_action.pre_state: When no usable nested gateway route is selected and top-level model configuration contains base_url or api_mode without provider, the canonical reader returns a partial route while billing_provider is stored separately; bare billing buckets are not routable identities.
semantic_action.post_state: The canonical reader preserves nested-route precedence, preserves explicit top-level provider and endpoint fields, fills only a missing top-level provider from a routable billing_provider, and still filters bare billing buckets.
semantic_action.validation: The shared reader is exercised through the target CLI/Desktop route-equivalence test and the existing endpoint-hygiene regression; the pinned commit does not add a standalone test dedicated only to the top-level-endpoint-without-provider branch.

candidate_atomics.name: resume_via_canonical_route
candidate_atomics.description: Align the Desktop/TUI stored-session adapter with the canonical route resolver so the current model is restored with the route that last served it instead of being paired with the first-call billing provider.

semantic_action.intent: Restore a gateway-driven session on a coherent current provider/endpoint/wire route and remove the stale-provider 404 caused by recombining fields from different route snapshots.
semantic_action.pre_state: The gateway has persisted the current route under nested gateway_runtime and the row model may reflect that route, but the Desktop/TUI reader ignores nested runtime metadata and falls back from an absent top-level provider to the first-accounted billing_provider; the CLI already uses the canonical reader.
semantic_action.post_state: Desktop/TUI resume obtains provider, base_url, and api_mode from the canonical route reader, giving nested gateway_runtime precedence over stale top-level keys and billing_provider while preserving the stored model and existing downstream endpoint/provider healing.
semantic_action.validation: The two pinned regression tests prove the main end-task oracle: nested gateway route beats stale billing_provider, Desktop matches CLI for the same row, and nested route fields beat stale top-level provider/endpoint fields.

candidate_atomics.name: route_precedence_regression_oracle
candidate_atomics.description: Add focused stored-row tests that make cross-surface route precedence observable and prevent future recombination of a current model with an older provider or endpoint.

semantic_action.intent: Detect regressions in provider, endpoint, and wire-mode precedence during Desktop/TUI and CLI session restoration.
semantic_action.pre_state: A persisted row can contain a current model, a first-call billing provider, stale top-level route keys, and a newer nested gateway route; without explicit assertions these fields can silently be mixed.
semantic_action.post_state: Focused tests require Desktop/TUI and CLI to restore the nested route as a coherent tuple and require nested route data to override stale top-level route data.
semantic_action.validation: `test_resume_honors_gateway_runtime_over_first_call_billing_provider` asserts nested-route restoration and CLI/Desktop parity; `test_resume_prefers_gateway_runtime_over_stale_top_level_keys` asserts nested precedence over stale top-level fields; the issue evidence reports both as red on base and green on head.

candidate_workflows.description: Establish one canonical persisted-route precedence contract, make Desktop/TUI resume consume it, and validate that a session's current model is restored with the latest coherent provider/endpoint/wire route.

workflow_graph.goal: Resume a gateway-driven session on the route that last served its current model, avoiding a 404 caused by pairing that model with the first-accounted billing provider.
